เมื่อวันพฤหัสบดีที่ ๒๑ ธันวาคม พ.ศ. ๒๕๖๐: On Thursday, 21 December 2017, in Grand Ballroom 1, Manee Chan Resort, Chanthaburi Province, at the 13th seminar on compiling the National Memory of the World Register, Mr. Kritsada Bunyasamit, Associate Fellow of the Academy of Moral and Political Sciences and Chair of the Committee for the Revision and Study of Ancient Thai Law, Office of the Royal Society, proposed registering the Three Seals Law as national and world documentary heritage in honor of King Phra Phutthayotfa Chulalok the Great, with Professor Sawaeng Bunchaloemwiphat as the discussant. The Three Seals Law is a compilation of Thai laws dating from the Ayutthaya period, which King Rama I ordered to be classified and revised. It was in use for more than 500 years and reflects the historical development of Thailand in politics, government, the economy, society, arts and culture. Only one set exists and it is irreplaceable, making it significant at both national and global levels
